proof_summary: Take \(K=(8r)!\). For \(r\le 4n\), Legendre’s formula together with a residue-class floor inequality proves \((2n)!(3n)!(4n-r)!\mid(8r)!n!(8n-2r)!\), and combining this with \((8n)!(4n-r)!=\bigl(\prod_{k<r}(8n-(2k+1))\bigr)2^r(4n)!(8n-2r)!\) gives the claim; for \(r>4n\), the absolute value of the product splits into two products of consecutive odd numbers, each controlled by a suitable factorial and hence dividing \((8r)!\).
